title: Alibaba Cloud Marketplace for APAC Sellers
summary: How Alibaba Cloud Marketplace works for APAC sellers: the vendor gate, the paid-product Cosell agreement, monthly settlement, and how it differs from AWS.
body_markdown:
*Alibaba Cloud Marketplace is the distribution channel where independent software vendors sell to buyers across the Asia-Pacific region and, through Alibaba Cloud’s China estate, into the market Western hyperscalers do not reach directly. It transacts real software revenue, but the vendor gate, the paid-product agreement, and the settlement clock work nothing like AWS, Azure or Google Cloud — and each difference is where an unprepared seller loses a month.*


---


An ISV team evaluating Alibaba Cloud Marketplace usually arrives with the AWS playbook in hand: register as a seller, build the listing, submit for review, take money when a buyer subscribes. They assume Alibaba is that same motion pointed at a different region.


It is not, and the gaps are not cosmetic. On Alibaba the ability to *publish* and the ability to *charge* are separated by a signed agreement. Payout is monthly, and the clock does not start when the customer pays — it starts when a finance form is complete. And the whole thing sits on an account model built for a company selling *into* China from outside it, which carries requirements no US-marketplace onboarding prepares you for.


Here is what the channel actually asks of an APAC seller, and where it diverges from the Western hyperscaler marketplaces.


---


## **What is Alibaba Cloud Marketplace?**


Alibaba Cloud Marketplace is an online catalog where vendors publish software and service products that buyers purchase alongside their Alibaba Cloud usage. It is Alibaba Cloud’s equivalent of AWS Marketplace or Azure Marketplace: a place to reach cloud buyers, transact through the platform, and settle revenue without standing up your own billing relationship in every country you sell to.


What makes it strategically distinct is reach, not mechanics. Alibaba Cloud is the largest cloud provider in China and a major one across the rest of APAC, so the marketplace is the practical route to a buyer base the three Western hyperscalers serve thinly or not at all. For an ISV whose expansion plan names Southeast Asia, Greater China, or the wider Asia-Pacific region, this is often the only marketplace where those buyers are already spending.


The seller-facing surface is the **Seller Portal** — the console where a vendor manages products, agreements, and the financial details that settlement depends on. Everything below runs through it.


---


## **How does the Alibaba Cloud Marketplace vendor model work?**


The vendor model has two gates, and they are not the same gate. **You clear the first with a vendor application; you clear the second by signing an agreement — and only the second lets you charge.** Teams that treat “we were approved as a vendor” as “we can sell paid software” lose the time it takes to discover otherwise.


To become a vendor at all, Alibaba Cloud requires a **Business Account** registered on alibabacloud.com, a secure mobile phone bound to the account, your company legal name exactly as it appears on your business license, and the business license itself uploaded during the application. You fill in the required fields, submit the application, and receive a confirmation email. This is a company-identity review, not a self-service toggle — Alibaba is verifying a real registered business behind the vendor.


That identity requirement is the first thing that surprises a US-based ISV. The account is a business account, the phone number requirement is stated relative to China mainland, and the qualifying document is a business license rather than a tax ID. None of that maps onto the AWS seller-registration flow, and it is the kind of localization work that belongs on the plan early, not discovered at submission.


Once registered, what you may publish depends on the second gate:


Product path What it covers What it needs


Free products No-charge listings for reach and evaluation Vendor registration complete


BYOL products Bring-your-own-license — the buyer licenses from you outside the marketplace Vendor registration complete


Paid products Products the marketplace charges for and settles to you The Cosell Agreement, signed online


Alibaba Cloud states it plainly: you can publish Free and BYOL products after registration is complete, and to publish paid products you sign the Cosell Agreement online. So a vendor who wants marketplace-billed revenue has a specific, non-optional step between “registered” and “selling” — and it is a contract, not a form.


---


## **How does settlement and payout work on Alibaba Cloud Marketplace?**


Settlement is monthly and automated, and it depends on a finance form more than it depends on the sale. **Alibaba Cloud settles ISV earnings monthly through an automated online system — but the payout clock starts when your financial information is complete, not when the customer pays.** This is the single most common place a first sale sits unpaid.


The mechanism is documented directly. Alibaba Cloud settles ISV earnings monthly through an automated online system, and vendors must update their financial information in the **Finance Center** of the Seller Portal, because that information “is used for invoice generation and payment settlements.” The consequence is stated just as plainly: incomplete or pending financial information delays the settlement timeline.


Read that as an ordering rule. Finance Center completion is not post-launch housekeeping you get to later — it is a prerequisite that gates when money can reach you. A vendor who publishes, wins a buyer, and only then opens the Finance Center will typically watch a completed sale wait for the following month’s settlement cycle. The fix is trivial and the miss is expensive: complete the Finance Center before the first order, not after it.


This is the mirror image of how the hyperscaler marketplaces feel to a seller. On AWS or Azure, the payout mechanics fade into the background once you are registered; on Alibaba, the finance step is a discrete gate you can fail silently, because nothing stops you from selling with it incomplete — it only stops you from being paid on time.


---


## **How is Alibaba Cloud Marketplace different from AWS and Azure?**


Alibaba differs from the Western hyperscaler marketplaces on the axis that costs a seller the most time: **what stands between “registered” and “getting paid.”** On AWS or Azure that gap is essentially a listing review; on Alibaba it is a company-identity application, a separate paid-product agreement, and a finance-form prerequisite for payout. Everything an APAC seller should plan around descends from those three.


Alibaba Cloud Marketplace AWS / Azure Marketplace


Listing model Free and BYOL after registration; paid products behind a signed agreement Register, then list free or paid products; paid gated at listing review


Seller entity / localization Business Account, business-license verification, phone requirement stated relative to China mainland Company seller registration, tax and banking details, no China-specific identity step


Gate to charge Sign the Cosell Agreement online for paid products Complete tax/bank profile; no separate paid-product contract to sign


Payout Monthly automated settlement; starts on Finance Center completion Disbursed on the marketplace’s schedule once the seller profile is complete


Primary buyer reach APAC and China, where the Western hyperscalers are thin North America, EMEA, and the rest of the world


Regulatory footprint Selling into China-adjacent markets carries local data, licensing and tax considerations you assess with counsel Governed by each marketplace’s standard seller terms


The practical consequence for an ISV: an Alibaba listing is not a regional copy of your AWS listing. The packaging may translate, but the *onboarding* does not — the entity verification, the paid-product agreement, and the settlement prerequisite are all new work that a completed AWS or Azure listing does not prepare you for. Budget it as a separate track, not a port. For how each of the smaller marketplaces gates sellers differently,[selling on Snowflake, Oracle and Alibaba Cloud](https://www.suger.io/resources/blog/selling-on-snowflake-oracle-and-alibaba-cloud/) covers all three side by side.


One caution that sits outside the marketplace mechanics: selling into China and China-adjacent markets carries data-residency, licensing and tax questions that vary by jurisdiction and by what your product does. Those are real, and they are not something a marketplace onboarding flow decides for you — treat them as a legal and compliance workstream you run in parallel, informed by counsel who knows the region.


---


## **Where does Alibaba Cloud fit in a multi-marketplace GTM?**


Alibaba Cloud belongs in a multi-marketplace GTM wherever your buyers already run on Alibaba Cloud — which is a *different* buyer than your AWS or Azure buyer, concentrated in a region the Western hyperscalers do not serve well. **The sequencing question is not “which marketplace is biggest,” it is “where is this customer already spending,” and for a Greater China or APAC account the answer is frequently Alibaba and nowhere else.** A product with real demand in that region belongs on Alibaba regardless of where else you sell.


That does not make Alibaba a replacement for the hyperscaler marketplaces; it makes it the surface that reaches a buyer the others miss. Many vendors end up on both — the AWS or Azure listing captures the buyer provisioning on a Western hyperscaler, and the Alibaba listing captures the APAC or China account that never appears in those consoles. They rarely cannibalize each other because they reach different customers in different regions.


The operational trap is the one every additional marketplace sets: running Alibaba as its own project, with its own console, its own catalog, its own agreement tracking, and its own reconciliation. That is what makes the fifth marketplace cost as much as the first. The fix is one catalog, one offer model, and one place transactions reconcile across all of them — with Alibaba’s vendor-registration, Cosell-agreement, and Finance-Center specifics handled inside that single operating model rather than as a separate manual effort.

## **Frequently asked questions**


**What is Alibaba Cloud Marketplace?** Alibaba Cloud Marketplace is an online catalog where vendors publish software and service products that buyers purchase alongside their Alibaba Cloud usage. It is Alibaba Cloud’s equivalent of AWS or Azure Marketplace, and the practical route to buyers across APAC and China that the Western hyperscalers serve thinly.


**Who can sell on Alibaba Cloud Marketplace?** A registered business that completes the vendor application: a Business Account on alibabacloud.com, a bound secure mobile phone, your company legal name matching your business license, and the license uploaded. Alibaba verifies a real registered company behind the vendor before approving it.


**How do you sell a paid product on Alibaba Cloud Marketplace?** Registration alone lets you publish Free and BYOL products. To publish paid products the marketplace charges for and settles to you, Alibaba Cloud requires signing the Cosell Agreement online. It is a separate, non-optional step between being a registered vendor and selling paid software.


**How does payout work on Alibaba Cloud Marketplace?** Alibaba Cloud settles ISV earnings monthly through an automated online system. Payout depends on completing your financial information in the Finance Center of the Seller Portal, which is used for invoicing and settlement. Incomplete or pending financial information delays the settlement timeline.


**How is Alibaba Cloud Marketplace different from AWS Marketplace?** The gap between registering and getting paid is wider. Alibaba adds a company-identity vendor application, a separate signed agreement for paid products, and a Finance Center prerequisite before payout. An Alibaba listing is new onboarding work, not a regional copy of an AWS listing.


**Does Alibaba Cloud Marketplace reach buyers in China?** Yes — that reach is its main strategic value. Alibaba Cloud is the largest cloud provider in China and a major one across APAC, so its marketplace serves a buyer base the Western hyperscalers do not. Selling there also carries local data and tax considerations to assess with counsel.


---


## **Takeaways**


- Alibaba Cloud Marketplace is the practical route to APAC and China buyers the Western hyperscalers serve thinly — reach is what makes it strategically distinct, not the mechanics.
- Being an approved vendor is not the same as being able to charge. Free and BYOL products publish after registration; paid products require signing the Cosell Agreement online.
- The vendor gate is a company-identity review: a Business Account, a business license, and a phone requirement stated relative to China mainland — none of which the AWS or Azure onboarding prepares you for.
- Settlement is monthly and automated, but the payout clock starts at Finance Center completion, not at the sale. Complete it before the first order.
- Treat an Alibaba listing as new onboarding work, not a regional port of an AWS listing — and run the China-region data, licensing and tax questions as a parallel legal workstream.
- Run every marketplace off one catalog and one reconciliation surface, so the fifth marketplace does not cost what the first did.
